items.title: A closure was a receiver of a `Callable` struct's impl: `twice.call(5f)` on a closure `|n: f64| n * 2f` beside `impl Scale with Callable { fun call(self, n: f64): f64 }` compiled to `Scale`'s `call` with the closure as `self` and printed `NaN`
items.body: `impl_subject_admits` asked `compare_type`, whose B340 arm admits a closure against a `Callable` value of the same shape (the coercion into a closure slot). Asked of an impl SUBJECT that is the wrong question - the same one the trait-object rule in `impl_subject_admits` already answers for `dyn`. Every shape-matching closure was in reach of the struct's members, and std's own `type_is_callable(|T| R)` answered yes through any package's callable struct (kolt's `Scale`), which is what refused kolt's client the std prefix (M145's second refusal). Fixed: an impl on a struct or enum head admits no closure or function receiver; pinned by `callable::a_closure_is_no_receiver_of_a_callable_structs_impl` and `a_callable_struct_still_coerces_into_a_closure_slot`. Estate 0. NOTE for solver-52: the change is in `impl_subject_admits` (inference).

items.title: M110 S6/S7's per-source path keys were off by one: std's `lib.vl` (and a dependency's surface) registered a source without pushing its key into `id_windows.source_keys`, so every later source was keyed by the NEXT source's path and the last by `0` - the demand table and the item-record keys of every package module named the wrong file
items.body: Item records stayed sound only because the text hash and the signature validate a served record; two files with an identical item text could have collided under a shifted key. The entry-module arm of the drain also pushed a key for a source it did not register. Each source now registers its own key beside it, debug-asserted (`source_keys.len() == sources.len()`) at the build's source-path seam.

items.title: M137's one-`Expr::Local(parameter)`-per-(node, context) sharing collides with the native backend's F31 liveness: `last_uses` is a set of READ entity ids, so one shared reference entity read by two threaded calls in one function would mark both reads the binding's last use and move the hidden context value twice
items.body: M137 asked to check first that no emitter memoizes by argument entity; vilan-rust does (`compute_liveness` overwrites a candidate per binding and inserts the surviving READ id; `copy_a_consumed_place_read` elides the copy for an id in `last_uses`). Doors: exempt `context_hidden_parameters` reads from F31's candidates (they are handles; measure the copies it then takes), or mint per (call, context) only where a function threads more than once and share the rest. Not built in Order 52.

items.kind: question (owner) - M146's dependency half, not built
items.title: Dependencies 'hot like the package' (M146's rec, ruled for P2) needs `load_hot_modules` to carry the drain's whole dependency machinery - per-package namespaces and `LoadedPackage` edges, the dependency `lib.vl` surfaces and their walks, per-package preludes, `package_of_source`, `dependency_sources`, the platform-layer re-export gate, `ModuleKey::Dep` expansion - none of which the hot-load path has; P2 still refuses `dependencies`
items.body: The estate's one dependency program is `examples/fullstack`. Two doors: (a) as ruled, port the dependency arms into the hot load (L; the differentials on fullstack and a hand-written two-package fixture); (b) a dependency TIER in the prefix: the drain already loads `Origin::Dep` requests (S1 loads a hot module's dependency requests into its prefix today), so the prefix becomes std + dependencies keyed by the std closure, the workspace fingerprint and the package's dependency requests, and only the package is hot. Rec: (b) - it reuses the drain, matches the tier order (std, dependencies, package), and a dependency is not edited in the editor session that the prefix serves.

items.discussion: incr-52b (Order 52); kolt @dee494ab built with and without VILAN_STD_PREFIX=on
items.title: The const-site cache's keys depend on the world's SHAPE: kolt built over the forced std prefix writes `dist/.cache/const-sites` with 109 of its 113 keys different from a canonical build's, though the emitted bundle is byte-identical and each build is deterministic run to run
items.body: `const_cache::site_key` hashes the `Debug` rendering of the lowered declarations, which carries ids; a prefix world numbers its entities differently (std's walk before the package's module nodes). Harmless today (layering is the server's, whose const cache is per process; the CLI builds canonically), but a cache shared across shapes misses wholesale, and std-prefix P3's persisted world will need a const key that is a function of content, not of ids.
